title: Output map preserves communication complexity
statement: Let $p$ be a private-coin finite-message protocol with input types $X$, $Y$, private-randomness types $\Omega_X$, $\Omega_Y$, and output type $\alpha$, and let $g \colon \alpha \to \beta$ be any function. Then the protocol obtained by running $p$ and applying $g$ to its output has the same communication complexity as $p$, i.e. $\mathrm{complexity}(\mathrm{map}\,g\,p) = \mathrm{complexity}(p)$.
hypotheses_covered: a private-coin finite-message protocol p over input types X, Y, randomness types Ω_X, Ω_Y, and output type α
replaced:
Mapping a function over the output of a protocol does not change its communication
complexity: $(p.\mathrm{map}\;g).\mathrm{complexity} = p.\mathrm{complexity}$.
